business_problem: CNH struggled to analyze large-scale geospatial agricultural data because tens of thousands of polygons were ingested daily and the prior environment could not efficiently turn them into actionable crop insights.
solution_summary: CNH centralized large-scale geospatial analytics on the Databricks Data + AI Platform so agricultural and construction data could be analyzed at the scale needed for product and crop insights. Databricks ingests tens of thousands of polygons each day and stores them in Delta Lake, giving the company ACID guarantees and elastic performance as field-level observations are combined with broader regional and global trends. Unity Catalog adds fine-grained governance, while collaborative notebooks let engineers and analysts remove roadblocks quickly and keep data quality high. CNH also uses the built-in H3 indexing system and Databricks spatial library to run geospatial aggregations that were previously impractical, helping teams analyze crop conditions and weather patterns faster. What once took a full day now runs in about two hours, enabling daily refreshes, lower compute and storage costs, and wider access to geographic insights without requiring specialized geospatial expertise.

data_flow: Geospatial polygons and other agricultural datasets are ingested into Databricks and stored in Delta Lake, where Unity Catalog governs access for collaborative teams. H3-based and spatial-library processing then aggregates the data into crop and weather insights that feed refreshed daily reports and downstream analysis.
business_outcome: CNH cut geospatial analysis time from a full day to two hours, enabled daily refreshes, lowered storage and compute costs, and made crop-condition reporting accessible to more users without requiring specialized geospatial expertise.
